newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi vice-president to attend Rome food summit.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi vice-president to attend Rome food summit.

text.p: An Iraqi vice-president left for Italy on Sunday to attend a global food summit as part of Iraq's effort to push forward a stalled oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
Taha Mohieddin Ma'rouf left Baghdad to attend the World Food Summit sponsored by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) which opens in Rome on Wednesday, the official Iraqi News Agency said.

"He will meet with heads of states and delegations attending the conference to explain the impact of the unjust embargo and their role in alleviating the suffering of the Iraqi people by ending the shortage of food and medicine," it said.
Iraq has been under U.N. trade sanctions since it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
Baghdad signed a deal with the United Nations in May allowing it to sell $2 billion worth of oil in six months to buy food and medicine. The agreement has yet to be implemented.

INA also said Trade Minister Mohammed Mahdi Saleh had travelled to Ankara to attend meetings of an economic and trade cooperation committee affliated to the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC).
